description:
FILED s484a (Opus, 2026-09-13) from the #1587 acceptance probe (rows 02/04/05).
PRE-EXISTING for the plain spelling: `eval 'package Foo2;'` answers "Foo2" on
main 2ffefb36 too.  #1587 only extended the same behaviour to the two
spellings that used to be REFUSED, so the divergence is now uniform across
all three rather than uniform across one.

    perl 5.40.3          PCL
    eval 'package Foo2;'          undef     Foo2
    eval 'package Ver4 1.2;'      undef     Ver4
    eval 'package Ver5 1.2'       undef     Ver5
    eval 'package Foo1; 1'        1         1        (ok -- a real trailing stmt)
    eval 'package Blk6 { 1 }'     1         1        (ok -- s484a's prog1)

A `package NAME;` statement is a compile-time declaration with no run-time
value, so when it is the LAST statement of an eval the eval's value is undef.
PCL's eval-region collapse lowers the statement into the statement stream,
where `p-set-current-package` is an ordinary call whose value -- the package
name -- becomes the region's tail.

This is the SAME MECHANISM s484a fixed for the BLOCK form, where it was
visible as `eval 'package X { 42 }'` answering "main" (the restore call's
value) instead of 42: `_lower_block`'s block arm now puts the restore behind a
`prog1`.  The statement form's twin fix is the mirror image -- when the
`package NAME;` statement is in a TAIL position with no statements after it,
its lowered form must not be the value.  The `@enter` forms are already
hoisted out of the run stream for the eval region (`_eval_pkg_enter`), so what
is left in tail position is whatever `_lower_block(\@rest, â¦)` returns for an
EMPTY @rest; that is the place to answer undef instead.

NOT MERELY COSMETIC: the eval's value is what `my $ok = eval "package $pkg;"`
tests, and a truthy package name where perl gives undef flips such a test.
t/op/packagev.t asserts `$@` rather than the value, so no measured row sits
behind this today -- which is why it is filed rather than fixed in s484a.

BAR: the seven-spelling table in scratch/s484a/probes/p1587.pl (rows 01-07,
where 02/04/05 are the divergent ones and 01/03/06/07 must not move), a guard
row beside the #1587 rows in Pl/t/parser2-02.t, corpus-diff + emission-ab (an
emission change), and the gate-set scan if the tail lowering changes for file
mode too -- it must not: at file level a `package NAME;` statement's value is
never read.
SIZE: S.
subject: `eval 'package Foo;'` returns the package NAME where perl returns undef -- a trailing `package NAME [VERSION];` statement has no value in perl, and PCL gives it one
